scope.topic: Mitosis: duplicated chromosome alignment and sister chromatid separation in eukaryotic cells
scope.organism_context: eukaryotic cells (animal cell examples with centrosomes/centrioles; plant/fungi differences noted but not modeled)
included_processes: prometaphase kinetochore attachment and chromosome orientation
metaphase alignment at the metaphase plate
anaphase sister chromatid separation and poleward movement
excluded_processes: prophase nuclear envelope breakdown and centrosome separation
simplifications: Only one duplicated chromosome (one sister chromatid pair) is modeled; the source's 'all chromosomes' statements are instantiated for this single pair only. The alignment observable checks that this one modeled duplicated chromosome is at the metaphase plate, explicitly delimiting it as an instantiation of the universal source statement.

Separation is represented by the joined sister-chromatid pair splitting into two distinct persistent daughter chromatid entities (each now called a chromosome), each moving toward an opposite pole. The post-separation identity is carried by these two daughter chromatid entities, not by the whole pair.

The molecular mechanism by which the sister-chromatid connection breaks down (cohesin degradation/cleavage) is not modeled; only the observable breakdown of the connection is asserted, and no causal sufficiency of microtubule pulling alone is claimed.
Processes are discrete stages for schematic clarity; the after/concurrent_with links represent schematic phase order, not strict per-chromosome mechanistic causal prerequisites.
Maximal chromosome condensation at metaphase is noted in source but excluded from process effects as out-of-scope for alignment/separation proof.

processes.scientific_name: prometaphase kinetochore-microtubule binding and bipolar chromosome orientation

preconditions.kinetochore_formed: Each sister chromatid has a kinetochore in the centromeric region.
preconditions.spindle_microtubules_present: Mitotic spindle microtubules are present and extend from centrosomes.

effects.attachment: Kinetochore microtubules from opposite poles attach to the two sister chromatids at their kinetochores.
effects.orientation: The chromosome is oriented so that the kinetochores of the sister chromatids face opposite poles.
effects.mechanism_note: Binding is asserted as source-supported; the attract-and-bind description is schematic only.

processes.scientific_name: metaphase alignment of the duplicated chromosome at the metaphase plate

preconditions.bipolar_attachment: Sister chromatids attached via kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.
preconditions.cohesin_present: Sister chromatids still tightly attached to each other by cohesin proteins.

effects.alignment: The modeled duplicated chromosome is aligned at the metaphase plate.
effects.scope_note: Source states 'all the chromosomes' align; only the single modeled chromosome is instantiated. Maximal condensation noted in source but excluded from this proof.

temporal_scope.start_condition: Chromosome has achieved bipolar kinetochore attachment.
temporal_scope.end_condition: Chromosome is aligned at the metaphase plate.

support.quote: all the chromosomes are aligned in a plane called the metaphase plate
During metaphase , the “change phase,” all the chromosomes are aligned in a plane called the metaphase plate , or the equatorial plane, midway between the two poles of the cell.

processes.scientific_name: anaphase breakdown of sister-chromatid connection and poleward movement of daughter chromatids

preconditions.metaphase_alignment: Duplicated chromosome aligned at the metaphase plate (schematic phase order; not asserted as a strict per-chromosome causal prerequisite).
preconditions.bipolar_attachment: Sister chromatids attached via kinetochores to microtubules from opposing poles.

effects.connection_breakdown_observed: The connection between the sister chromatids breaks down as an observed transition; the molecular cause (cohesin degradation/cleavage) is out of scope and not modeled.
effects.separation: The two sister chromatids become two distinct daughter chromatids (now called chromosomes).
effects.poleward_movement: The microtubules pull the daughter chromatids toward opposite poles; no causal sufficiency of microtubule pulling alone for the connection breakdown is claimed.

temporal_scope.start_condition: Duplicated chromosome aligned at metaphase plate with bipolar kinetochore attachment (schematic phase order).
temporal_scope.end_condition: Sister chromatids separated into two distinct daughter chromatids moving toward opposite poles.

support.quote: In anaphase, the connection between the sister chromatids breaks down, and the microtubules pull the chromosomes toward opposite poles.

precondition.metaphase_alignment: Duplicated chromosome aligned at metaphase plate (schematic phase order).
precondition.cohesin_present_prior: Sister chromatids still tightly attached by cohesin proteins prior to anaphase.

support.quote: Each chromatid, now called a chromosome, is pulled rapidly toward the centrosome to which its microtubule is attached.
During anaphase , the “upward phase,” the cohesin proteins degrade, and the sister chromatids separate at the centromere.
In anaphase, the connection between the sister chromatids breaks down, and the microtubules pull the chromosomes toward opposite poles.

exceptions.note: Source also states 'the cohesin proteins degrade' (paragraph_30); this molecular mechanism is acknowledged but deliberately not modeled as a causal agent. The process asserts only the observable breakdown and separation; no causal sufficiency of microtubule pulling alone is claimed.

unresolved_questions.question: The exact molecular mechanism by which the sister-chromatid connection breaks down (e.g., cohesin cleavage by separase) is not modeled; only the observable breakdown is asserted, and no causal sufficiency of microtubule pulling alone is claimed.
Precise timing and duration of prometaphase, metaphase, and anaphase are not specified in the retrieved passages.
Whether the spindle assembly checkpoint is required for anaphase onset is not explicitly stated in the retrieved passages.
Whether phase order (metaphase alignment before anaphase separation) constitutes a strict per-chromosome mechanistic precondition is not explicitly stated; modeled as schematic phase order only.
